questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 40.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

questions.questionText: Eukaryotic organisms grow and increase in size as a result of cell division. The diagram shows some stages of mitosis with one stage missing, labelled X. X What happens in stage X?

options.A: Spindle fibres attach to the centromeres and the chromosomes line up along the equator.
options.B: The chromatin coils and condenses and the nuclear membrane disintegrates.
options.C: The chromosomes line up in pairs along the equator of the cell.
options.D: Microtubules shorten so that spindle fibres contract and the centromeres divide.

questions.questionText: The graph shows how changes in oxygen concentration affect the percentage oxygen saturation of human haemoglobin and cat haemoglobin under normal physiological conditions. The partial pressure of carbon dioxide was kept constant at 5.0kPa and the temperature was kept constant at 37C. 100 human cat percentage saturation of haemoglobin with oxygen partial pressure of oxygen Which conclusion is supported by the graph?

options.A: The affinity of cat haemoglobin for oxygen is greater than the affinity of human haemoglobin for oxygen.
options.B: At high partial pressures of oxygen, cat haemoglobin picks up oxygen more easily than human haemoglobin picks up oxygen.
options.C: At low partial pressures of oxygen, oxygen is released more easily from cat haemoglobin than from human haemoglobin.
options.D: The shift in the oxygen dissociation curve caused by the Bohr effect is larger for cat haemoglobin than for human haemoglobin.

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct about how oxygen combines with haemoglobin?

options.A: Combining all four oxygen molecules with haemoglobin does not affect the shape of haemoglobin.
options.B: One oxygen molecule can combine with each haem group of the haemoglobin molecule.
options.C: The first oxygen molecule to combine with haemoglobin does not affect the shape of haemoglobin.
options.D: The third oxygen molecule to combine with haemoglobin makes it more difficult for the fourth oxygen molecule to combine with haemoglobin.

A scientist investigated the effect of an antibiotic on the treatment of cholera. 320 people with cholera were divided into two groups. One group was treated with the antibiotic while the other group was not given the antibiotic. Both groups were given fluids containing sugars and mineral salts (oral rehydration therapy). The scientist recorded the number of days that each person had diarrhoea. The table shows the results. mean time person had treatment diarrhoea/days antibiotic and oral rehydration therapy 3.2 oral rehydration therapy 5.3 What is the percentage decrease in the mean time that a person had diarrhoea when they were treated with the antibiotic?
How does the antibiotic penicillin affect the metabolism of a bacterial cell?

options.A: Penicillin reduces cell growth by preventing water uptake.
options.B: Penicillin inhibits the formation of cross-links in the cell wall between peptidoglycan molecules.
options.C: Penicillin inhibits the hydrolysis of peptidoglycan links in the cell wall during cell extension.
options.D: Penicillin weakens the cell wall by digesting peptidoglycan molecules.

questions.questionText: Scientists studied the multidrug-resistant bacterial infections in children caused by one type of bacteria between 2007 and 2015. The percentage of multidrug-resistant infections rose from 0.2% to 1.5%. What was the percentage increase in multidrug-resistant infections between 2007 and 2015?

Whooping cough is a highly infectious disease of the gas exchange system, caused by the bacterium Bordetella pertussis. Which method provides protection to infants against whooping cough and reduces the chance of developing this disease later?

options.A: a short course of more than one type of antibiotic
options.B: a six-month course of one type of antibiotic
options.C: injections of antibodies specific to Bordetella pertussis
options.D: injections of antigens from Bordetella pertussis bacteria

options.B: The cell synthesises a large quantity of proteins.
options.C: The cell synthesises large quantities of antigens.
options.D: The cell digests pathogenic bacteria.

options.B: It allows B-lymphocytes to synthesise antibodies.
options.C: It allows neutrophils to carry out phagocytosis.
options.D: It allows T-lymphocytes to recognise foreign antigens.
